mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.0% and remains above for at least two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.10 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 5% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which boosts wage growth and corporate pricing power, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not statistically higher than baseline during periods of tight labor markets (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) for two consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue expectations for cyclically-sensitive sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is below 0.05 over a 5-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production growth rate above 0.5% for three consecutive months signals an acceleration in economic output, which supports earnings growth and boosts equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth > 0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly above baseline during periods of accelerating industrial production (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of higher rates and inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed their 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of dual-trigger months, or the negative rank IC is below 0.08 over a 4-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above 6% over two consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports wage and profit growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE both > 6% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not statistically higher than baseline during periods of strong labor market expansion (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent YoY decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) for four consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which negatively impacts construction and materials sectors and drags on S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines YoY for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of sustained housing starts decline (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly GDP growth rate (GDPC1, quarterly annualized, interpolated monthly) below 1% for two consecutive months signals weak aggregate demand, which reduces earnings expectations across sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is below 0.06 over a 5-year window.
